body:
> After #6468, which changed the log level from info to debug [...]

Note that `debug` is a lower log level than `info`, i.e., whenever `debug` messages are printed, `info` messages are printed as well.

>  the repository rule results are printed on every build command, even when they have not changed. 

That I cannot reproduce (see example below). Debug information from the repository rules is only printed if it is advisable to change the definition of the repository rule (either directly in the `WORKSPACE` file, or by using a resolved file); will change the message to make this more obvious. In your example, bazel points out the following.

- A file is downloaded without a checksum being specified. Downloading files without verifying integrity can be a security issue; providing a hash also improves caching.

- A `git_repository` is used for a specific commit, but no reference date is given. Specifying a reference date allows users of the same `WORKSPACE` file to clone in a shallow way.

And here the example that I believe shows that the debug messages do not occur on a clean `WORKSPACE` file.

```
$ cat WORKSPACE
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
  name =  "ext",
  strip_prefix = "ext",
  urls = ["file:///memfs/tmp/ext.tar"],
  sha256 = "0761dc172c9704c2b1c0bee3cb8346c2d37cb147e62b63274f0d4fbb2b0e226f",
)
$ bazel build @ext//...

$ # remove checksum
$ ed WORKSPACE

d
```

> Note that `debug` is a lower log level than `info`, i.e., whenever `debug` messages are printed, `info` messages are printed as well.

Despite this being true in the order of `EventKind` and in general, it seems not that easy to disable debug messages. That seems a different issue.

issue.title: Log repository_rule result as debug

labels.name: team-ExternalDeps
labels.description: External dependency handling, remote repositiories, WORKSPACE file.

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Beginning with b42734f4213e505d9582def4cd25bd510f0909a9, `git_repository` and `new_git_repository` return a dictionary which is used to make reproducible builds via `--experimental_repository_resolved_file`. However this return value is logged at an `info` log level, which generates a lot of output for a project that uses many git repositories. Here's some example output: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/kastiglione/a289a10c05f67b2954a087d265935629/raw/c46e08723814cda10e0e26ef9622fdb466f49736/bazel-build.txt

This changes the log `.info` to `.debug`.

body: Let's rework the messages here to explain better what is meant: the suggestion to users abot how to make their repo rules more reproducible.

Ah, thanks for pointing out that I have not fully specified my repository rules, I will add checksums / shallow dates. I'm just surprised this was not being printed out on every build in 0.21. Was there another change recently?

>  I'm just surprised this was not being printed out on every build in 0.21. Was there another change recently?

94e1dcc99373f24d042624d72800223c03e98825 added the ability of `http_archive` rules to report the checksum of the file actually downloaded, so 0.22 is the first bazel release to actually indicate missing checksums for `http_archives`; the recommendation of adding checksum for security and caching reasons is much older, however.

Great to see the fix in a117ddf! It would be even better if we print the attributes to add/modify not in JSON-like format (`{ "attr1" : "value1", "attr2" : 2 }`) but in the format directly copy-pastable to WORKSPACE file:
```
attr1 = "value1", 
attr2 = 2
```

So I see that the fix re-words this log statement, but what's the recommendation to eliminate them entirely? Should we be submitting patches upstream to lock the versions and validate their shas? For example if you include buildifier inside bazel, these repositories print this log https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_go/blob/346de0cb6de6af7e71b746070aea9e0b469d509d/go/private/repositories.bzl#L38-L65

I've tried using a resolved file from master, but I'm seeing other issues with that, is that an alternative as well?
